headline: On last trading day, Sensex tumbled nearly 1,000 points as heavy selling in IT stocks dragged indices down.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 30 November.

why: Profit booking following a two-day market rally.
Sharp selling pressure in major IT sector stocks.
Market catching its breath after a 15% rally over four weeks.
Lingering global risks regarding US Federal Reserve interest rate hikes.
whatHappening: Sensex crashed nearly 1,000 points while Nifty 50 dropped below the 25,650 mark in the last session.
IT stocks led the market sell-off while metal stocks outperformed the broader market.
Gold prices rebounded from 15-month lows while silver prices surged nearly 6%.
Bombay High Court cleared the way for the Tata Sons board meeting scheduled for November 30.
summary:
In the last trading session, Indian benchmark indices snapped a two-day rally as the Sensex dropped nearly 1,000 points and Nifty fell below 25,650.
The steep market fall was driven primarily by aggressive selling in IT stocks alongside widespread profit booking.
In contrast to the equity market decline, metal stocks held up and precious metals like gold and silver rebounded strongly.
